thread:
ash: Hey team — running into intermittent 401s when using the Edge Node SDK from a service worker on Vercel. Seems like the preflight sometimes drops the Authorization header.
maria: Can you paste a minimal repro + which SDK version?

ash: Using @redwood/inference-js v0.9.2 on Vercel Edge (edge runtime). Simple service-worker style edge function that proxies to https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat. Locally with vite preview it works, but prod on Vercel I see intermittent 401s. Minimal code:
```js
addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  const TOKEN = process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN;
  event.respondWith(
    fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ input: 'hi' }),
    })
  );
});
```
Sometimes the browser's main request is sent without Authorization because the OPTIONS preflight returns without the right headers.

jules: Are you running as an Edge Function or middleware? Vercel has different behavior for middleware/service-worker-like code. Also any bundler transforms?

ash: Edge Function (not middleware). Bundling with Vite + @vercel/adapter. Build log shows a couple of esbuild warnings. Tried both credentials: 'include' and mode: 'cors' on the client side — no effect.

platform-eng: Can you dump the OPTIONS response headers from the server (or from Vercel)? Often the issue is a missing Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.

ash: Here is a sample OPTIONS response we captured from prod:
```
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
access-control-allow-origin: https://app.example.com
access-control-allow-methods: POST, OPTIONS
access-control-max-age: 3600
```
Note: Access-Control-Allow-Headers is missing (and Credentials header).

maria: That explains it — browser won't send the Authorization header for the actual POST if the preflight doesn't explicitly allow it. Does the origin return these headers for OPTIONS when hit directly (bypassing Vercel CDN)?

ash: Locally, origin returns the correct headers. On prod it looks like Vercel/edge returned a canned 204 without the allow-headers. Also saw some 429s on OPTIONS in the Vercel router logs which line up with the failing requests.

devx-bot: FYI there was a change in v0.9.0 where the SDK switched to an internal streaming fetch wrapper (it now uses globalThis.fetch differently). If your bundler polyfills fetch or rewrites it, the header handling can differ in service worker contexts.

jules: Another angle — some CDNs and edge routers will reject Authorization on preflight unless Access-Control-Allow-Headers is present. If Vercel returns a cached OPTIONS response (missing headers), the browser will never send the auth header. That matches the intermittent behavior (cache/cold vs origin hit).

ash: I also tried sending the token as a query param — that avoids the preflight problem but is a security no-no. Auth via cookie (httpOnly) seems to stop the problem, but we don't want to move tokens to cookie if we can avoid it.

platform-eng: Next steps: 1) collect a HAR from the browser repro showing the OPTIONS and POST pair, 2) export the Vercel logs for the same timeframe (include x-request-id or similar), 3) attempt curl to the edge URL forcing an OPTIONS to see the raw headers. If you can attach those we can open a Vercel support case and/or file an internal doc.

ash: Will gather HAR + Vercel logs and share here. One weird additional data point: when Vercel returns a 429 on OPTIONS, sometimes the POST goes through but without Authorization and hits the origin as anonymous — hence intermittent 401s. Looks like a race where failing preflight leaves a cached/no-auth path.

maria: For immediate mitigation, two options:
- Ensure your origin always returns Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, etc. (fixes proper preflight).
- If you control the edge layer, make it pass-through OPTIONS responses from origin (avoid cached canned 204s).
We should also document that SDK versions that change fetch behavior can interact poorly with certain bundlers + edge runtimes.

jules: Also try pinning to v0.8.x of the SDK to see if the behavior changes (customers reported fewer preflight surprises on the older wrapper).

support-bot: Created ticket S-2026 to investigate Vercel edge preflight/Authorization mismatch. Assigned to platform-eng.

ash: Thanks — I'll attach HAR + logs to S-2026. Temporary workaround: move auth to cookie for user sessions (stabilized prod). Not ideal but unblocks.

platform-eng: We'll follow up after Vercel log analysis. If it is a Vercel router bug, we'll escalate. Also adding this to devex doc backlog to warn about edge preflight races.

maria: I'll draft a short note for devex covering 1) required CORS headers for Authorization, 2) SDK bundling caveats (vite/esbuild) + pin suggestions, and 3) example server OPTIONS response to copy/paste.

ash: Appreciated. Will report back with artifacts. :thumbsup:
